hotspots.name: Madagascar
hotspots.fullName: Madagascar and the Indian Ocean Islands
description: An island apart, where evolution took its own path. Lemurs move through the canopy, chameleons cling to branches, and ancient baobabs punctuate the dry western forests.

From humid eastern rainforests to the spiny south, an extraordinary mosaic of habitats shelters life found nowhere else. Forest clearance and fragmentation leave these ecosystems increasingly isolated.
hotspots.habitat: Tropical forest · Mangrove · Coastal & reef-adjacent · Grassland · Desert
hotspots.conservation: Community-led protection and forest restoration are keeping Madagascar’s irreplaceable habitats connected.

hotspots.name: Tropical Andes
description: Cloud forests rise into high páramo grasslands along the spine of South America. Steep slopes and isolated valleys create a remarkable variety of ecological niches.
Changes in elevation bring striking changes in plant and animal communities. Forest corridors connect these habitats, but agriculture, mining and warming temperatures are reshaping them.

hotspots.name: Sundaland
description: Towering dipterocarp forests, peat swamps and mangrove shores weave through Borneo, Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula. This is a landscape shaped by water and dense tropical canopies.
Orangutans depend on connected forest for food and movement. Logging, plantation expansion and peatland drainage place pressure on the region’s extraordinary diversity.

hotspots.name: Atlantic Forest
description: A forest that follows the Atlantic, from misty mountains to warm coastal lowlands. Its remnants shelter golden lion tamarins, orchids and an exceptional diversity of trees.
Much of the original forest now survives in separate fragments. Restoring links between them helps wildlife move, disperse seeds and sustain the next generation of forest.

description: Seasonal forests and great rivers shape the landscapes of mainland Southeast Asia. Floodplains, limestone outcrops and mountain forests support distinct communities of life.

hotspots.name: Western Ghats
description: Monsoon forests, upland grasslands and streams shelter distinctive amphibians and plants. Mountain isolation has encouraged many small-range species.
Plantations, development and fragmentation alter the remaining habitat. Conserving forest and freshwater connections protects these ecological refuges.

hotspots.name: East Australian forests
description: Coastal and mountain forests span warm subtropical to temperate conditions. Eucalypt woodlands and rainforest remnants shelter distinctive communities.
Habitat clearing and changing fire patterns affect native wildlife. Connected reserves and restored forest help support recovery.

hotspots.name: Coastal Plain
description: Longleaf pine savannas, wetlands and coastal landscapes hold a rich native flora. Fire and water sustain the region’s distinctive ecological patterns.
Development and the loss of natural fire regimes reshape these habitats. Conservation includes restoring processes alongside protecting land.
